title: Quantitative Modeling of Action-Potential-Driven Sodium Dynamics in Neurons: From Sodium Influx to Sodium MRI
html:
Abstract:Neuronal action potentials are accompanied by the influx of extracellular sodium ions (Na+) into axons through voltage-gated sodium channels. Repetitive neuronal firing can lead to activity-dependent increases in intracellular sodium concentration, which are subsequently reversed primarily through the Na+/K+-ATPase. Quantifying these dynamic changes provides a biophysical foundation for investigating neuronal activity using sodium (23Na) magnetic resonance imaging (MRI). This mini-review examines the relationships among firing frequency, action-potential-driven sodium influx, and intracellular sodium accumulation, to establish a quantitative framework linking neuronal activity to sodium MRI. The potential sensitivity and limitation of conventional and compartment-sensitive sodium MRI for detecting activity-dependent sodium changes are also discussed. Keywords: Sodium MRI; neuronal firing; action potential; sodium influx; intracellular sodium concentration.
